questions.stem: During the electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide (Al2O3), aluminium is produced at the cathode and oxygen at the anode. Which half-equation correctly represents the cathode reaction?

options.text: Al -> Al3+ + 3e-
Al3+ + 3e- -> Al
Al3+ - 3e- -> Al

questions.explanation: At the cathode, reduction occurs. Aluminium ions (Al3+) gain 3 electrons each to form aluminium atoms: Al3+ + 3e- -> Al. Option A shows oxidation (the reverse). Option C shows the anode reaction. Option D uses incorrect notation for gaining electrons.

questions.stem: In the industrial extraction of aluminium, cryolite is added to the aluminium oxide before electrolysis. What is the main reason for this?

options.text: Cryolite acts as a catalyst to speed up the electrolysis
Cryolite lowers the melting point of aluminium oxide, reducing energy costs
Cryolite provides extra aluminium ions for electrolysis
Cryolite prevents the carbon anodes from reacting with oxygen

questions.explanation: Pure aluminium oxide has a very high melting point (about 2072 degrees C). Dissolving it in molten cryolite lowers the operating temperature to about 950 degrees C. This massively reduces the energy costs of keeping the electrolyte molten, making the process economically viable.

questions.stem: When molten calcium chloride (CaCl2) is electrolysed, what products form at each electrode?

options.text: Calcium at the anode; chlorine at the cathode
Calcium chloride gas at both electrodes
Calcium at the cathode; chlorine at the anode
Hydrogen at the cathode; oxygen at the anode

questions.explanation: In molten CaCl2, the ions present are Ca2+ and Cl-. Calcium ions (positive) migrate to the cathode and are reduced: Ca2+ + 2e- -> Ca. Chloride ions (negative) migrate to the anode and are oxidised: 2Cl- -> Cl2 + 2e-. Hydrogen and oxygen only appear in aqueous electrolysis where water is present.

questions.stem: In the electrolysis of aluminium oxide, the carbon anodes need regular replacement. Why?

options.text: The aluminium corrodes the carbon anodes
The carbon anodes react with the oxygen produced, forming carbon dioxide, and gradually wear away
The high temperature causes the carbon to melt
Aluminium deposits on the anodes and makes them too heavy

questions.explanation: Oxygen gas is produced at the anode. At the high operating temperatures, this oxygen reacts with the carbon anodes: C + O2 -> CO2. This gradually burns away the carbon electrodes, so they must be replaced regularly. This is a significant ongoing cost in aluminium production.

questions.stem: A student electrolyses molten lead(II) bromide and collects 20.7 g of lead at the cathode. How many moles of bromine gas would be produced at the anode? (Ar: Pb = 207, Br = 80)

options.text: 0.2 mol
0.1 mol
0.05 mol
0.01 mol

questions.explanation: Moles of Pb = 20.7/207 = 0.1 mol. The cathode half-equation is Pb2+ + 2e- -> Pb, so 0.1 mol Pb requires 0.2 mol electrons. At the anode: 2Br- -> Br2 + 2e-. To release 0.2 mol electrons requires 0.2 mol Br- ions, which produces 0.1 mol Br2. So 0.1 mol of bromine gas is produced.
